title: How a Nuclear Reactor Makes Power

endcard.line: Footage: Tennessee Valley Authority (public domain). Picture: Trougnouf (CC BY 4.0)

segments.say: A nuclear power station boils water to spin a turbine, just like a coal one. Only the source of heat is different.

anim.title: Fission
items: A neutron hits a uranium atom
The atom splits and releases heat
They split more atoms: a chain reaction

segments.say: Inside the core, a neutron strikes a uranium atom and splits it. That releases heat and more neutrons, which split more atoms. This is a chain reaction.

anim.title: The fuel
items: Pellets stacked in long fuel rods

segments.say: The fuel is uranium, packed into small ceramic pellets, stacked in long metal rods and bundled together in the core.
Control rods soak up neutrons: push them in to slow the reaction, all the way in to stop it. A moderator slows neutrons so they keep splitting atoms.
The heat turns water into steam. The steam spins a turbine, the turbine drives a generator, and the steam is cooled back into water.
Cooling towers like this one, or river and sea water, do that job.

anim.title: India's workhorse: the PHWR
items: Heavy water as coolant and moderator

segments.say: Most of India's reactors are pressurised heavy-water reactors. Heavy water is such a good moderator that they can run on natural uranium, without enriching it.
For GS Three: fission, heat, steam, turbine. And heavy water is what lets India use natural uranium.

sources: US EIA, 'Nuclear power plants': fission splits uranium atoms, releasing heat and neutrons in a chain reaction; fuel is uranium ceramic pellets stacked in 12-foot fuel rods; heat makes steam that spins turbines driving generators; cooling towers or water from lakes, rivers or the ocean
US EIA, 'Types of reactors': boiling-water and pressurized-water reactors
Wikipedia, 'Control rod' (read): control rods contain neutron absorbers such as boron or cadmium; inserting them controls the chain reaction; fully inserted they shut the reactor down
Wikipedia, 'Pressurized heavy-water reactor' (read): heavy water as coolant and moderator; natural uranium fuel; IPHWR-220 and IPHWR-700 are Indian designs

options: Absorb neutrons to slow or stop the chain reaction
quiz.why: They soak up neutrons; fully inserted, they stop the reaction.

quiz.q: What lets India's PHWRs run on natural uranium?
quiz.why: Heavy water is an efficient moderator, so enrichment isn't needed.

quiz.q: In a nuclear power station, what spins the turbine?
quiz.why: Fission heat makes steam; the steam spins the turbine.

reviewNote: Basics were read against two US EIA pages; control rods and the PHWR come from Wikipedia articles because NRC and NPCIL pages didn't return readable text here. 'Most of India's reactors are PHWRs' is not stated in those sources; check it against NPCIL's plant list before approval. The TVA animation is of a boiling-water reactor, which India doesn't use; it illustrates the steam cycle only. Start times (t) were chosen blind. Moving facts: India's reactor count.
